content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — cross-region routing anomalies detected. Elevated latencies and error spike for some US customers. Auto-page: @oncall.
Alyssa: seeing 5xx increase from US-east clients to /v1/generate, looks like a lot of traffic routed to eu-west.
Marco: confirmed, traffic heatmap shows ~40% of us-east requests hitting eu-west cluster since ~12:03 UTC.
Ingrid: dashboards show jump in avg p95 latency from 120ms -> 850ms for affected routes. Customers reporting timeouts.
Sam: any recent routing policy changes? I just merged a pinning tweak earlier but that was scoped to canary and rolled back automatically.
Marco: canary change was limited to dedicated, not global. Not sure link.
sre-lead: @Alyssa can you run a quick curl with x-region header to see what host responds?
Alyssa: running:
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1'
```
Alyssa: response header X-Redwood-Active-Region: eu-west-1
Nish: that suggests routing policy mapping is resolving incorrectly, maybe policy table picked eu-west as preferred for latency.
Ingrid: but latency measurements still show US nodes healthier. Something is skewing the telemetry that feeds routing decisions.
ops-bot: topology-change detected: geo-steer weight shift event (ID: gs-2026-03-15-001) at 12:02:48 UTC. Trigger: telemetry-input anomaly from regional probes.
Sam: is the telemetry anomaly a probe mislabeling? We had a probe agent rollout yesterday that touched probe tagging.
Marco: good call — the probe agent that tags region label rolled yesterday in eu-west and us-east; maybe tag mismatch.
Alyssa: immediate mitigation: can we override steer policy to prefer us-east for affected APIS?
sre-lead: pushing a temporary override. Command: `rbctl routing override --policy geo-steer --service api --force-target us-east-1 --ttl 60`
deploy-bot: route-override gs-override-1839994321 applied by sre-lead. Changes propagating.
Alyssa: confirming curl now shows X-Redwood-Active-Region: us-east-1 for the test. Latency back to ~140ms on quick sample.
Ingrid: still seeing a small number of sticky flows to eu-west due to DNS TTL and existing client connections. We'll need to drain.
Nish: digging into probe logs now — looks like probe in us-east temporarily reported region=eu-west (bad env var) between 11:58-12:03 UTC. That would make the steering controller think eu-west was faster.
Sam: root cause candidate: probe agent misconfiguration that set REGION_TAG=eu-west in us-east hosts. Who rolled that?
Marco: rollout scroll: probe-agent v1.4.2 pushed to us-east at 11:55 by infra-ops pipeline. Change included a templating tweak.
Alyssa: mitigation plan: 1) keep the routing override in place 2) rollback probe-agent template in us-east 3) set DNS low TTL to accelerate drain and force reconnection 4) coordinate on-call handoff after initial stabilize.
Ingrid: doing 2) now: `infra-deploy rollback probe-agent us-east to v1.4.1`
ops-bot: rollback job queued, started.
deploy-bot: rollback completed on 6/6 us-east hosts at 12:12 UTC.
Nish: probe logs after rollback show region tags consistent. Steering controller now getting correct telemetry.
Alyssa: setting dns TTL for api.redwood.ai from 300 -> 30 to speed recovery. Command run: `dns-cli set-ttl api.redwood.ai 30`
ops-bot: DNS TTL change pushed to global authoritative.
Marco: customer-impact summary: about 18% of production traffic from NA had elevated tail latency and ~2% 5xx rate spike over ~8 minutes window. Majority requests served but user experiences degraded. Top affected customers: two enterprise tenants with routing pinned to dynamic steering (IDs redwood-ent-43, redwood-ent-112).
hana (cs): I'm pinging CS for heads-up to those customers, will coordinate status page blurb once we have RCA.
Alyssa: monitoring: p95 back to baseline in 2 mins after override; 5xx dropping. Keep override for now until further verification.
sre-lead: post-mitigation tasks: - run full probe inventory for tag mismatches - revert DNS TTL to normal after drain - create a canary for probe env var templating - postmortem docs.
Marco: I'm starting a quick canary for the templating fix now.
Ingrid: handoff note for next oncall: we'll leave this as P1 mitigated. Override active (gs-override-1839994321) expires in 60m unless extended. Root cause likely probe agent mistemplating; full RCA pending.
Alyssa: handing off to @Nish for overnight monitoring, I need to hop to a customer call. Nish: you're on the thread.
Nish: got it, monitoring graphs and alert rules reviewed. I'll extend override if drift resurfaces.
Alyssa: thanks — adding a short runbook here:
- Check `rbctl routing status --policy geo-steer --service api` for active overrides.
- Validate probe-tags: `probe-inspect --list --filter region!=hostname_region`
- Watch 5xx and p95 on infra -> escalate to sre-lead if >2% 5xx sustained 3m.
Ingrid: updating incident channel with brief summary and ETA for RCA.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: P1 mitigated at 12:16 UTC. Override in place. RCA in progress.
hana (cs): posting proactive note to affected tenants and creating support tickets for impacted sessions.
Sam: retrospective action: we need test coverage on probe templating and a preflight validation in rollout pipeline to catch region-tag mismatches.
Marco: agreed. I'll open a Jira and link it here.
Alyssa: thanks all — handoff complete. Nish please ping if any drift. :thumbsup:
Nish: will do. Monitoring live and logs tailing.
Ingrid: closing thread for active coordination but will append RCA when done.
__notes: This thread captures an incident involving cross-region routing misdirection due to probe agent misconfiguration, the live mitigation steps (routing override, rollback, DNS TTL change), paging and on-call handoff. The file is named with a timestamp prefix per agents.md rules.
